population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever-users are 19.0% of adults and current users 10.7%, so 8.3 pts used and are off now. About 5.8 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈2.2 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again. (5.8+2.2)/19.0 = 42% cycled. That still fits ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year; MariTide's monthly dosing is too new to move it. Current users ≈ 28.6M of ~267M adults. The age bands, weighted by adult population shares (20/33/24/23%), come to ≈10.8%. Income thirds average (15.0+10.0+7.1)/3 = 10.7. Ever-use rose 2.5 pts. New starters come mostly from outside weight management: ASAM-guideline AUD prescribing, the 2029 smoking-cessation label, and low-dose 'quiet mind' and metabolic orals among 18–49s. That is why 18–29 rose from 4% to 5% and 30–49 from 10% to 11%. 50–64 fell from 19% to 18% because employers dropped weight-only coverage and postmenopausal women were warned about bone loss. 65+ held at 8% under Bridge rules that now require DEXA. The bottom third rose from 6.5% to 7.1% almost entirely through mail-order Indian and Canadian pens (≈2.6M users, under-measured). The middle third is flat at 10% because people who lost employer coverage were roughly offset by those moving to cash. Off-drug population: ~22M adults who used and are off now, often regained and without bone follow-up; ~216M who never used, concentrated among the uninsured, the bottom third, and a small but visible 'off by choice' group under 35. Pediatric: ~0.4% of under-18s (≈290k), mostly adolescents 12+. The oldest continuously treated adolescents now have about 7 years of exposure, and there are still no bone-accrual data.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: CMS rolled it over administratively in Oct 2029 through Dec 2031 on unchanged terms. Medicare pays ~$245/month, the copay is $50, criteria are the same, and the counselling visit is still required; the 2029 bone guidance adds a baseline DEXA for women 65+. ≈1.5M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 1.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.4B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈19% of fills ≈ 5.4M users (≈8% of ~63M adults 65+ ≈ 5.0M, plus ~0.4M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈10% ≈ 2.9M users at $245: 2.9M × $245 × 12 ≈ $8.5B/yr federal plus state. Coverage varies by state, and the Indiana and Arkansas adherence-gated waivers are unchanged.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 70+ generic semaglutide brands at $8–45/month, plus first generic liraglutide-semaglutide oral combinations. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 70–100/month. Generics are also sold in Brazil, Mexico, Turkey, China and Egypt. Ex-US generic tirzepatide is not yet available. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices are still stalled. TrumpRx/direct cash is ~$245–350 for injectables and $149 for oral starting doses; Wegovy lists at $1,349 and retatrutide at $1,499 with no cash programme. MariTide (Feb 2030) lists at $1,299, with an Amgen direct price of $599 for a monthly in-clinic dose. Payer mix of ~28.6M users: commercial 38% (10.9M), Medicare 19% (5.4M), Medicaid 10% (2.9M), cash/direct 24% (6.9M), gray/imported 9% (2.6M) = 100% ≈ 28.7M. Employer retreat: the share of employers covering weight management fell from 58% to 49%. Most of those still covering have moved to code-gated coverage, paying only with a T2D, established ASCVD, OSA, MASH or CKD diagnosis. About 60% of commercial fills now carry one of those codes, up from ~45%. Two tiers are now firm. One is coded patients, with plan-paid drug, DEXA and monitoring. The other is everyone else paying $149–350 cash, or $8–45 for imported pens that come with no prescriber oversight. About half of the employers that still cover weight management use adherence-gated PBM programmes, and they favour MariTide because a single monthly administration is easy to verify.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Survodutide was approved in Jan 2029 on its pending filing and is used mainly where MASH is present. Amycretin was approved Aug 2029, 14 months after its Jun 2028 NDA, at ~22% loss. MariTide was in phase 3 with no filing at the start of the window. Amgen filed the BLA in Nov 2028 and FDA approved it in Feb 2030 as the first monthly incretin, at ~17–20% mean loss over 72 weeks. Launch supply limits it to ≈0.7M users by end-2030, and it is given in clinic or by monthly self-injection. No implant is on the US market; an osmotic-pump exenatide revival is in phase 2. This launch is how the monthly_or_implant driver is realised. Retatrutide allocation eased in 2029. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) entered phase 3 in 2029 and none can be approved before 2031–32. Incretin market ≈$114B in 2030: US volume is up and prices are flat, ex-US generic erosion continues, and new-agent launches add modestly.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; more salient with retatrutide.

Recognised as a population problem. A pooled US–Nordic cohort (2029) puts sarcopenia criteria in 65+ users on therapy >2 years at ~1.5–1.7× matched non-users, and extends a smaller excess (~1.2×) to long-term users aged 50–64. Lean-mass share of loss is ~25–40%.

food_and_beverage.state: Snack and sugary-drink volumes are still eroding at about 2026–28 rates. Protein, fibre and calcium claims are standard. The backlash has opened a small counter-niche of 'real food, no apology' and heritage-recipe branding. Supplement makers selling 'natural GLP-1' berberine and fibre blends are growing fast off the same anti-pharma current.

alcohol.state: Contracting faster. The AUD guideline endorsement brings GLP-1s into addiction clinics and EAPs, sober-curious users dose for drinking, and cessation coverage adds a nicotine cohort. restaurants.state: Traffic is steady. Small plates and protein-forward menus are standard. Some independents in Austin, Brooklyn and Atlanta explicitly market abundance ('the full plate') to the backlash crowd.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide because sizes move both ways. Plus-size specialists stabilise as employer-retreat regainers return, and the fat-acceptance revival brings back body-positive marketing that had been dropped in 2025–26.

fitness.state: Still growing on the bone and muscle wave. DEXA-plus-coaching chains are in strip malls nationwide and Medicare Advantage strength benefits are common. Some chains administer MariTide in-house through partner clinics, turning a monthly visit into a training membership.

insurance.state: Employers covering weight management fell from 58% to 49%, with coverage concentrated on diabetes and cardiac codes. Pharmacy trend has eased to ~+6% as weight-only volume shifts to cash. Plans that still cover push MariTide plus adherence gating as their cost-control story.

pharma.state: Market ≈$114B. Lilly leads with retatrutide, Foundayo and tirzepatide. Amgen enters with monthly MariTide. Novo is stabilising after a 2029 settlement of the securities suits, while the DOJ matter remains open. US prices are flat and ex-US revenue keeps eroding to generics. The 2031–32 US exclusivity cliff is now the sector's main planning issue.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among coded, insured professionals over 40, being on the drug is still normal. A second reading has emerged, however: visible regain now usually means 'employer dropped coverage', and a sizeable minority of under-35s treat an unmedicated body as a statement. The 'on it too long' look of thin arms and stooped posture in older users is widely recognised, and DEXA results get discussed the way cholesterol numbers once were.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The gradient keeps widening: 15.0% of the top third use, against 7.1% of the bottom third. The top third uses low-dose orals, MariTide in clinic and DEXA with coaching. The middle third without a qualifying code moved to $149–350 cash or stopped. Much of the bottom third's use is imported pens with no monitoring. In Dallas–Fort Worth's insurance and banking workforce, two large carriers dropped weight-only coverage in January 2030, and lunch counters that sold protein by the gram now sell a 'regain-friendly' bowl as well.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller shared meals and protein-first eating are still the norm. The backlash has brought back abundance as ritual: potlucks, Sunday suppers, and church 'Daily Bread' dinners that explicitly welcome unmedicated appetite. In Tulsa, a Southern Baptist megachurch network's supper programme draws thousands weekly under a 'bodies are not a diagnosis' framing.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list 'on', 'off' or 'off by choice'. The last is now a values signal, much as 'sober' once was. Mismatched appetites in mixed couples are a standard topic for advice columns.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: There are two readings. In clinics and HR, appetite is still something to manage. A visible counter-movement treats it as health and moral agency. It draws on three sources: a fat-acceptance revival among women 20–35, MAHA-adjacent 'natural' wellness influencers selling berberine, and church groups. The coalition is unstable, but its slogans ('Feed the whole person', 'My hunger isn't a disease') are everywhere.

interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is a marketing term: albums, a Nashville songwriters' showcase and comedy specials advertise being recorded off the drug. interior_life.effect_on_politics: It shows up as cost, control and identity. The India/Canada price gap is a bipartisan stump line. The counter-movement unites fat-liberation activists on the left with 'natural health' activists on the right, against pharma and against BMI surcharges, but they agree on little else. BMI-linked wellness surcharges up to 30% of premium remain legal and are a focus of the backlash.

Manufacturers cite Section 232 tariffs and the coming 2031–32 cliff as reasons not to cut. Amgen's MariTide is made in the US and Ireland.

prose.headline: Your Boss Stopped Paying, Your Bones Are Thinning, and Your Daughter Thinks You're a Sellout: The Shot at 2030
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 a little over one American adult in ten is on an incretin drug, about 28 million people. That is slightly more than two years ago, although the people paying for it are different. Prices have not moved. Injectables cost $245 to $350 a month through the federal cash portal, oral starting doses cost $149, and Wegovy still lists at $1,349. The industry's explanation is tariffs, and behind that the 2031 patent cliff, which nobody wants to pre-empt with a price cut. Employers have stopped waiting. Since January 2029 enough of them have dropped weight-only coverage that fewer than half now pay for it. Most of those still paying will only cover a patient with a diagnosis code: diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea, a fatty liver. A two-tier system has formed. People with a code get the drug, a bone scan and a coach. People without one pay cash, stop, or order Indian generics by mail at the price of a sandwich. About 2.6 million Americans now take pens that no American prescriber has seen.

Growth comes from somewhere else: the brain. In 2029 semaglutide won a smoking-cessation label, and addiction-medicine guidelines endorsed it for alcohol use disorder. Telehealth companies sell low-dose pills to twenty- and thirty-somethings who were never heavy, as a 'quiet mind' or a focus aid. The FDA has sent letters objecting to that language, but has not stopped the prescriptions. Use among adults under thirty has risen by a quarter.

The same quieting is now an ordinary complaint. 'Flat' is common slang. Roughly a third of weekly users say they skip or halve doses for holidays, gigs, deadlines or anniversaries. Albums advertise being recorded off-dose. Sex therapists ask about dosing intervals. Amgen's MariTide, approved in February as the first monthly shot, complicates this. Its long-tail dose cannot be skipped, so a drug holiday has to be planned a month ahead. Trucking fleets, which still need drivers on tirzepatide to clear sleep-apnea screening, are among its first buyers and give the injection at the depot. The plans that still check adherence prefer it for the same reason.

The bone problem has also grown. A pooled study of four million users confirmed that older long-term users break hips more often. It extended a smaller excess to women in their fifties and to people who cycle on and off. Cycling is now known to rebuild the body with more fat and less muscle each time. With employer coverage ending abruptly for millions, that cycling has increased. DEXA chains in former mattress stores are booked weeks out, and Medicare now requires a scan for older women.

Not everyone wants the drug. A counter-movement that would have seemed impossible in 2025 has formed. It brings together young women reviving fat acceptance, natural-health influencers selling berberine as 'nature's version', and church supper networks like one in Tulsa whose slogan is 'bodies are not a diagnosis'. In October 2029 they filled parks in a dozen cities. They disagree about almost everything except their opponents: the industry, BMI surcharges on insurance premiums, and the idea that hunger is a defect. 'Off by choice' is now a dating-profile category.

Policy has barely changed. Medicare's $245 Bridge was rolled over, Indiana and Arkansas still cut off Medicaid users who miss two weigh-ins, and no new rule was written. Snack makers have adapted, spirits makers keep shrinking, and plus-size stores are selling to people regaining weight. From the outside the country looks steady. The open questions are who owns the steadiness, and how many people are taking unchecked pens, with untracked bones, waiting for 2031.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Harlan, fifty-seven, sits in the DEXA chair at FormLab in Plano, where the mattress store used to be, while a technician in a lanyard reads her a number with a minus sign in front of it.

"Osteopenic," he says. "Not osteoporosis. Lift twice a week. Here's the package."

The package is $89 a month. The Zepbound vials are $349 since Lone Star Mutual took her off the plan in January, and her A1c of 5.9 is not a code. She checks her banking app in the car.

At lunch Priya from claims eats a fourteen-gram protein bowl and slides her phone across: a pen from Pune, $38 delivered, two months now, nobody's asked. "Customs took one box. They sent another."

Denise eats half her bowl and wraps the rest.

At seven her daughter Kayla arrives with a lasagna because it is Kayla's birthday and Kayla is twenty-four and off by choice. Her T-shirt says FEED THE WHOLE PERSON. She cuts Denise a square without asking.

"One night, Mom. Be hungry with me."

The vial is in the refrigerator door behind the mustard. Wednesday is shot day. It is Wednesday.

Denise eats the lasagna slowly. It is very good, and she remembers that it used to be better. She laughs at something Kayla says about a boyfriend and notices herself laughing, which she hasn't done in a while.

After Kayla leaves she opens the refrigerator, looks at the vial, and closes the door again. She opens her laptop. The Pune site has a chat window. A cartoon pharmacist waves.

She puts her hand on her hip, the one the scan circled, and leaves the tab open.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare's $245 Bridge was rolled over, Indiana and Arkansas still cut off Medicaid users who miss two weigh-ins, and no new rule was written.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world state says the Bridge now requires a baseline DEXA for women 65+, and the prose says 'Medicare now requires a scan for older women'. That is a new benefits rule, so the 'no new rule' line contradicts it and strains the state_action: none driver.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Cycling is now known to rebuild the body with more fat and less muscle each time.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the safety ledger lists the body-composition ratchet as 'emerging', with data that only 'suggest' it and no formal regulatory response. The prose upgrades it to settled knowledge, so prose and world state disagree.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Some fleets are moving drivers to MariTide, administered at the depot.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the DOT sleep-apnea requirement is tied to tirzepatide's OSA indication, and MariTide has no OSA label. Fleets also could not plausibly switch within months of a February 2030 launch with supply capped near 0.7M users.

rationale.badness: Employer retreat has pushed the middle and bottom thirds into cash or unmonitored imports (~2.6M users) and into abrupt cycling that the fracture and body-composition data link to the worst outcomes. Inequality is the worst dimension, and the fracture signal now reaches women 50–64. Autonomy is mixed because employer steering weakened and the Indiana and Arkansas waivers persist. Harms are more nameable than in 2028 (SHAPS data, DEXA culture, the body-composition ratchet), and the backlash is both a fracture line and a source of community, so cohesion and epistemic stay mid-range.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visibly realised: the 10.7% adoption figure, flat prices, employer coverage 58→49%, AUD and 'quiet mind' indications, the 2029 pooled bone cohort, the MariTide launch, the 'Full Plate' backlash, and 'flat' as slang. The Bridge DEXA requirement and 'no new rule' wording slightly strain state_action: none, and the Novo settlement is only a mild brush with market_shock: none. mechanism: Most chains are shown (employer retreat → code-gating → cash/imports → cycling → fracture), but claims 1–3 are weak links. They are the 'no new rule' contradiction, the ratchet overstated as 'known', and the fleet switch to MariTide with no OSA label. magnitude: Current use 10.7% and ever-use 19.0% are inside the envelope. The cycling arithmetic (8.0/19.0 ≈ 42%), the age-band weighting (≈10.8%), and the payer mix (sums to 100%, ≈28.7M) all reconcile. Medicare at ~5.4M and Medicaid at $8.5B reconcile too. Survodutide, amycretin and MariTide are each approved ≥12 months after filing, and there is no US generic. The only blemishes are the loose attribution of the bottom-third rise to imports and the 2.5-point ever-use jump.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third rose from 6.5% to 7.1% almost entirely through mail-order Indian and Canadian pens (≈2.6M users, under-measured).
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude. A 0.6-point rise in a ~89M-adult third is only ~0.5M extra users, while gray-market use grew by ~1.3M to 2.6M in total. The 'almost entirely' attribution does not reconcile with the payer-mix and income-third figures.

least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism and driver_fidelity. The same world has the Medicare Bridge rolled over by CMS in Oct 2029 and newly requiring a baseline DEXA for women 65+. That is a benefits rule, so the section contradicts itself on the state_action: none driver.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Cycling is now known to rebuild the body with more fat and less muscle each time.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism (narrative contradiction). The safety ledger lists the body-composition ratchet as 'emerging', with data that merely 'suggest' it and no formal regulatory response, so 'now known' overstates the world state.

rationale.badness: The two-tier coded/uncoded system (`access.note`), ~2.6M unmonitored imported-pen users, abrupt coverage-driven cycling, and fracture and sarcopenia signals now reaching women 50–64 make a recognisably harder society. Inequality is worst (top third 15.0% vs bottom 7.1%, DEXA and coaching for the coded only). Autonomy partly improves because employer steering weakens, though the Indiana/Arkansas gating and monthly-dose institutional administration persist. Reward blunting is still unmeasured as a harm, and the AUD/cessation framing keeps the epistemic score middling.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible and traceable. The adoption delta lands at exactly +0.8, employer coverage falls 58→49%, MariTide is a filing plus approval, the AUD and 'quiet mind' indications appear, the bone and muscle wave extends to women 50–64, and backlash and mainstream complaint are both realised. The one tension is that a CMS rollover and a new Bridge DEXA rule sit awkwardly with state_action: none (claim 2). mechanism: Most changes have chains: coded coverage, cash shift, gray market, and employer steering fading into self-titration. The weak points are the overstated cycling-ratchet claim in prose (claim 3), the loosely evidenced church-network petition scale, and the convenient left/right backlash coalition. magnitude: All headline figures sit inside the envelope (10.7% current, 19.0% ever, income thirds bracket the national figure, age bands weight to 10.8%). Approvals are at least 12 months after filing, the payer mix sums to 100%, and the Bridge ($4.4B) and Medicaid ($8.5B) arithmetic checks out. The one gap is the bottom-third rise attributed to a 2.6M gray market (claim 1).
rationale.generativity: The Denise/Kayla/Priya scenes carry strong texture: the DEXA chair in a former mattress store, the Pune pen, FEED THE WHOLE PERSON, and the vial behind the mustard. The world fields add Tulsa suppers, depot-administered MariTide and sex therapists asking about dosing interval, so many further scenes are implied. The film potential is high, though some details lean on tidy symbolism.

least_plausible_claims.quote: India: 70+ generic semaglutide brands at $8–45/month, plus first generic liraglutide-semaglutide oral combinations.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: liraglutide is a daily injectable peptide, and an oral fixed-dose combination of two GLP-1 agonists is pharmacologically incoherent. It is also an unexplained invention with no causal chain from the parent world.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Cycling is now known to rebuild the body with more fat and less muscle each time.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the prose states as settled something the world's own safety ledger lists as 'emerging', based on 'DEXA-chain and cohort data suggest'. This is a narrative-versus-state contradiction.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Some fleets are moving drivers to MariTide, administered at the depot.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the DOT sleep-apnea route runs through tirzepatide's OSA indication, and MariTide has no such indication. Employer-administered injections within months of approval and under 0.7M supply are asserted rather than shown.

rationale.badness: The world has a firm two-tier system: coded patients get the drug plus DEXA, while everyone else pays cash, stops, or uses unmonitored imported pens (~2.6M). The bone and sarcopenia signal now reaches women 50–64, and coverage cut-offs drive abrupt cycling (access/note, safety_ledger). Reward blunting is a mainstream complaint, and the Indiana and Arkansas waivers persist. Weaker employer steering, visible DEXA discussion and the backlash movement give some autonomy and nameability back, so this is a harder society with new losers, not a structurally hidden harm.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Nearly all drivers are visible in the fields and events. Mood and motivation is realised only as off-label 'quiet mind' use with no filing, and the new Bridge DEXA requirement and FDA letters sit slightly awkwardly beside state_action 'none'. mechanism: Most chains are shown, for example employer retreat to code-gating to cash and imports, and monthly dosing to gated plans. Weak spots are the invented liraglutide-semaglutide combination, the overstated cycling claim, and the fleets-to-MariTide jump (claims 1–3). magnitude: Every figure sits inside the envelope (10.7%, 19.0%, income thirds averaging 10.7, age bands weighting to ≈10.8). The payer mix sums to 100%, Medicare and Medicaid dollars multiply out, the 42% cycling arithmetic reconciles, and all approvals respect the 12-month rule (amycretin 14, MariTide 15).
rationale.generativity: The Denise and Kayla scene is concrete: the FormLab DEXA chair, the vial behind the mustard, the Pune chat window, and the lasagna on shot day. The world fields add many implied characters and scenes, including Tulsa supper churches, depot injections, 'off-dose' albums and the 'off by choice' dating filter. Daily life has texture throughout.

least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world state says the Bridge now requires a baseline DEXA for women 65+, and the prose says 'Medicare now requires a scan for older women'. That is a new benefits rule, so the 'no new rule' line contradicts it and strains the state_action: none driver.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Cycling is now known to rebuild the body with more fat and less muscle each time.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the safety ledger lists the body-composition ratchet as 'emerging', with data that only 'suggest' it and no formal regulatory response. The prose upgrades it to settled knowledge, so prose and world state disagree.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Some fleets are moving drivers to MariTide, administered at the depot.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the DOT sleep-apnea requirement is tied to tirzepatide's OSA indication, and MariTide has no OSA label. Fleets also could not plausibly switch within months of a February 2030 launch with supply capped near 0.7M users.

rationale.badness: Employer retreat has pushed the middle and bottom thirds into cash or unmonitored imports (~2.6M users) and into abrupt cycling that the fracture and body-composition data link to the worst outcomes. Inequality is the worst dimension, and the fracture signal now reaches women 50–64. Autonomy is mixed because employer steering weakened and the Indiana and Arkansas waivers persist. Harms are more nameable than in 2028 (SHAPS data, DEXA culture, the body-composition ratchet), and the backlash is both a fracture line and a source of community, so cohesion and epistemic stay mid-range.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visibly realised: the 10.7% adoption figure, flat prices, employer coverage 58→49%, AUD and 'quiet mind' indications, the 2029 pooled bone cohort, the MariTide launch, the 'Full Plate' backlash, and 'flat' as slang. The Bridge DEXA requirement and 'no new rule' wording slightly strain state_action: none, and the Novo settlement is only a mild brush with market_shock: none. mechanism: Most chains are shown (employer retreat → code-gating → cash/imports → cycling → fracture), but claims 1–3 are weak links. They are the 'no new rule' contradiction, the ratchet overstated as 'known', and the fleet switch to MariTide with no OSA label. magnitude: Current use 10.7% and ever-use 19.0% are inside the envelope. The cycling arithmetic (8.0/19.0 ≈ 42%), the age-band weighting (≈10.8%), and the payer mix (sums to 100%, ≈28.7M) all reconcile. Medicare at ~5.4M and Medicaid at $8.5B reconcile too. Survodutide, amycretin and MariTide are each approved ≥12 months after filing, and there is no US generic. The only blemishes are the loose attribution of the bottom-third rise to imports and the 2.5-point ever-use jump.
